problem: VLM-based continuous VLN agents such as NaVid use all past RGB frames as memory. Memory and compute therefore grow linearly with episode length (276 MB at 300 steps for NaVid), and the history has no explicit spatial or semantic structure. Earlier semantic/grid maps for VLN are feature tensors or color-coded images that pretrained VLMs cannot read.
motivation: In continuous navigation (R2R-CE/RxR-CE), the agent must track where it has been and which landmarks it has seen, at a bounded memory cost. VLMs are pretrained on natural images and text. The observation driving the paper is that VLMs therefore understand a top-down map much better when semantic regions carry explicit text labels. Raw top-down maps, colored semantic maps and depth images are poorly understood and can even hurt.
key_idea: Replace the historical-frame memory of a VLM navigation policy with one constant-size top-down Annotated Semantic Map. The map is built online from RGB-D, pose and segmentation, and its object regions are labeled with text. It is fed together with the current RGB frame into a fine-tuned LLaVA-OneVision model that outputs actions as text.
insight:
The gain comes from making the map legible to the VLM's language prior, not from having a map as such. On R2R-CE val-unseen (Tab. 3), each map variant compares as follows against the no-map baseline (27.3 SR / 23.2 SPL):
- The simulator's original top-down map slightly hurts (26.4 / 21.9).
- An unlabeled multi-channel semantic map helps only a little (29.1 / 24.5).
- Adding centroid text labels (ASM) jumps to 36.5 / 34.3.

Feeding depth as an extra image also hurts (23.1 SR vs 27.1 RGB-only, Tab. 5), so inputs should match what the VLM was pretrained on. Other ablations:
- Data: DAgger data gives the largest gain (23.9 → 33.5 SR, Tab. 4); collision-recovery data beats adding RxR.
- History: extra RGB frames give diminishing returns on top of ASM (2 frames 39.7 SR; 4 frames ~41 SR / 38 SPL per Fig. 6 text).
- Segmentation: better segmentation helps (YOLOv8 31.5 < MobileSAM 34.8 < Mask2Former 36.5 SR).
method: Semantic map construction: at every step, egocentric depth + pose are back-projected to a point cloud and projected top-down into a C=n+4 channel egocentric-initialized map. The four base channels are obstacles, explored area, current position and past trajectory; n channels hold object categories. Object masks come from Mask2Former and are aligned with the point cloud. The map is initialized with the agent at the center (W/2, H/2) and updated each step.

Annotated Semantic Map (ASM): connected-component analysis runs on each object channel. For each region above an area threshold τ, a text label (e.g. 'chair', 'bed', 'plant') is placed at the geometric centroid. The result is a rendered image that includes the red trajectory line, so the VLM can ground it with its language prior.

Two-stream encoding on LLaVA-OneVision: a shared frozen SigLIP-so400M (384px, patch14) encodes the current RGB frame and the ASM image. Each stream goes through spatial-unpadded patch merging and its own 2-layer GELU MLP projector (P_obs, P_map). Tokens are assembled as [TASK; E_obs; OBS; E_map; MAP] plus instruction tokens into Qwen2-7B-Instruct.

Text action output + regex parsing: the LLM generates a natural-language action. Case-insensitive pattern sets map synonyms ('move forward'/'proceed', 'turn left'/'rotate left', 'stop'/'halt'/'wait', ...) to the discrete actions FORWARD / TURN-LEFT / TURN-RIGHT / STOP, so no separate action decoder is needed.

Training data pipeline: step-wise (RGB, ASM, instruction, action) pairs come from three sources: R2R/RxR ground-truth trajectories, DAgger rollouts of the pretrained model, and ~25k collision-recovery samples per dataset (~1M pairs total claimed). These are co-trained with ~600k LLaVA-OneVision general VQA / multi-image / video samples.
Optional short history: a variant appends 2 (or 1/4) historical RGB frames to the ASM + current RGB input.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-OneVision: SigLIP-so400M vision encoder (frozen) + 2-layer MLP projectors + Qwen2-7B-Instruct LLM (fine-tuned); Mask2Former for segmentation in ASM generation
setting.training_data: Step-wise SFT pairs of current RGB + ASM + instruction → action, from R2R-CE/RxR-CE. Sources: GT trajectories, DAgger rollouts and collision-recovery samples; the R2R model uses ~500k pairs (300k + DAgger + collision), with ~1M claimed in total across R2R+RxR. Co-trained with ~600k general vision-language samples (VQA, multi-image, video) from the LLaVA-OneVision mix. 1 epoch, lr 1e-6, 8×A100 for ~30 h.
setting.observation: Monocular egocentric RGB for the VLM, plus depth + agent pose, which are used only to build the ASM (Table 1 marks MapNav as Cur. RGB only despite this). An optional 2 historical RGB frames in one variant.
setting.action_space: Low-level discrete VLN-CE actions (FORWARD / TURN-LEFT / TURN-RIGHT / STOP), parsed from generated text
setting.privileged: None at test time beyond depth and agent pose/odometry for map building. Semantics come from Mask2Former, not ground truth. Only one ablation uses the simulator's GT top-down map ('Original Map').

numbers_note:
Internal inconsistencies:
- The main ASM + Cur. RGB model has NE 5.92 in Table 1 but 5.22 in all ablation tables (Tabs. 3-6), with the same OS/SR/SPL.
- The no-map baseline is 27.1/23.5 SR/SPL in Tables 1 and 5 but 27.3/23.2 in Table 3.

The historical-frame ablation (1/2/4 frames) is given only as a figure; the text gives rounded values (4 His. RGB: SR 41%, SPL 38%).

Other reported results not entered as benchmark rows:
- Dataset ablation (Tab. 4, R2R-CE val-unseen): 300k gives 23.9 SR / 19.5 SPL; 300k+DAgger 33.5/30.7; 300k+DAgger+RxR 34.4/31.7. The text also mentions a 100k configuration that is not in the table.
- Segmentation ablation (Tab. 6): YOLOv8 31.5/29.6; MobileSAM 34.8/31.6.
- RGB+Depth (Tab. 5): 23.1/19.9.
- Real-world results (Tab. 2): 5 rooms × simple/semantic instructions, 50 instructions total, SR in 10% steps. Examples: Lecture Hall semantic 70% SR / NE 1.15; Living Room semantic 60% / 0.85.

Training-set sizes are described inconsistently (300k vs 200k GT pairs; 500k vs ~1M total).
results:
On R2R-CE val-unseen, with only the current RGB frame plus ASM, MapNav reaches 36.5 SR / 34.3 SPL, close to NaVid with all historical frames (37.4 / 35.9). Against NaVid restricted to the current frame (13.0 / 7.8), it is 23.5 / 26.5 points higher.

Adding 2 historical frames and RxR training gives 39.7 SR / 37.2 SPL on R2R-CE and 32.6 SR / 27.7 SPL / 43.5 nDTW on RxR-CE. The paper claims SOTA over NaVid (RxR 23.8 / 21.2, though that was cross-dataset). It remains well below panoramic waypoint-predictor methods such as ETPNav (57 SR) and HNR (61 SR).

Memory stays constant at 0.17 MB versus 276 MB for NaVid at 300 steps, and per-step time drops from 1.22 s to 0.25 s. On a Unitree Go2 robot in 5 real rooms, it beats NaVid and WS-MGMap, e.g. +30% SR on semantic instructions in the lecture hall and living room.
limitations: Depends on semantic segmentation quality (Mask2Former > MobileSAM > YOLOv8), which degrades under occlusion and lighting changes. The method also needs depth and accurate pose to build the map, although Table 1 lists it as current-RGB-only.

The RxR comparison with NaVid is not like-for-like: the headline 2-frame MapNav is trained on RxR while NaVid's RxR numbers are cross-dataset. Absolute performance still trails panoramic waypoint-based VLN-CE methods by a large margin.
Real-world evaluation is small (50 instructions, 10 per room) and runs on an off-board A100 server. There are reporting inconsistencies (NE 5.92 vs 5.22 for the same model; dataset sizes).
